name: Frank J. Mrvan
gradeNote: SBA Pro-Life America grade F; Heritage Action 119th Congress score 0%; LCV lifetime score 97%. Voted for the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act, against the 2023 Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (did not vote on the 2025 version), and against the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act; campaign platform supports codifying Roe v. Wade.
description: Hammond native and former North Township trustee seeking a fourth term in the U.S. House.

name: Barb Regnitz
gradeNote: Newcomer to federal office; campaign site pledges to defend the right to keep and bear arms, strengthen border security, end reckless spending and reduce the national debt, and keep girls' sports and facilities for biological females. No public position on abortion found (left the iVoterGuide Right to Life item unanswered); endorsed by President Trump, Sens. Banks and Young, and Maggie's List.
description: Porter County commissioner (elected 2022) with a background in software engineering and financial planning.

name: Jamee Decio
gradeNote: Campaign platform calls for eliminating ICE's budget and disbanding the agency, a pathway to citizenship, and much higher taxes on billionaires; no stated positions on abortion, marriage, religious liberty or firearms were found.
description: South Bend attorney and former Elkhart County deputy prosecutor.

name: Rudy Yakym
gradeNote: SBA Pro-Life America A+; Heritage Action 119th Congress score 85%; LCV lifetime 1%. Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (2023 and 2025) and the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
description: Republican who has represented Indiana's 2nd District since 2022, campaigning on limited government, lower taxes and reduced regulation.

name: William Eric Henry
gradeNote: Told the Capital Chronicle he supports any reduction in taxes at all levels and downsizing government, and lists medical freedom and privacy as priorities; also backs federal cannabis reform. No stated positions on abortion, marriage, religious liberty or firearms were found.
description: Elkhart communications professional and military veteran making his third Libertarian run for the 2nd District (2022, 2024, 2026).

name: Kelly Thompson
gradeNote: Ballotpedia lists her affiliations as including Planned Parenthood and the ACLU; her platform calls for Medicare for All and a new tax on Wall Street trades to fund education. No stated positions on firearms or religious liberty were found.
description: Concrete contractor, nonprofit founder and former jail-ministry visiting pastor from North Webster; 2020 Democratic nominee for Indiana House District 22.

name: Marlin A. Stutzman
gradeNote: SBA Pro-Life America A+; Heritage Action 119th Congress score 100%; LCV lifetime 4%. Voted for the 2025 Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act and the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act; platform emphasizes cutting federal spending, border security, gun rights and limiting the federal role in education.
description: Howe farmer and business owner, former Indiana House and Senate member, who returned to Congress in 2024 after previously holding the seat.

name: Drew Cox
gradeNote: Ballotpedia survey states he supports codifying Roe v. Wade and passing the Equality Act, calls for abolishing ICE, higher taxes on the ultra-wealthy and reduced military spending; he also states that removing the right to bear arms has no place in a free political system.
description: Purdue University music instructor and Marine Corps veteran (2008-2012) from Lafayette.

name: Jim Baird
gradeNote: SBA Pro-Life America A+; Heritage Action 119th Congress score 84%; LCV lifetime 6%. Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (2023 and 2025) and the 2025 Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.
description: Farmer, small-business owner and Vietnam veteran seeking a fifth term; former Putnam County commissioner and Indiana state representative.

name: J.D. Ford
gradeNote: As a state senator, voted against SB 1, Indiana's 2022 abortion ban (July 2022 Senate vote), and said he would 'strongly oppose' it; supports codifying Roe v. Wade federally and criticized the 2025 federal tax-and-spending package. Other state votes on the six values were not reviewed.
description: Indiana state senator for District 29 since 2018 and the first openly gay member of the Indiana General Assembly.

name: Victoria Spartz
gradeNote: SBA Pro-Life America A+; Heritage Action 119th Congress score 92%; LCV lifetime 4%. Voted against the 2022 Respect for Marriage Act and for the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (2023 and 2025); she was one of two Republicans to vote against the September 2025 stopgap spending bill.
description: Republican who has represented Indiana's 5th District since 2021 and won a third term in 2024.
